why.text: How big is a piece of software, before any code exists? Function Point Analysis measures its functionality from the requirements, independent of the programming language.

app.text: Take the weather app from the slides. One input screen for temperature and rainfall by city and state. One database. One report.

ei.text: External inputs: data crossing the boundary from outside to inside. The add, change and delete buttons. Three.

eo.text: External outputs: derived data going out. The report, with its monthly averages. One.

eq.text: External inquiries: data retrieved. The scroll bar that shows previous entries. One.

ilf.text: Internal logical files: data living inside the application. The database. One.

eif.text: External interface files: another application's data, used for reference only. None here. Zero.

rank.text: Each one is ranked low, average, or high, by counting its fields and the files it touches. Here, everything is low.

ufp.text: Multiply each count by its weight. Three inputs times three. One output times four. One inquiry times three. One file times seven. Unadjusted function points: twenty-three.

vaf.text: Next, the general system characteristics. Each gets a weight from zero to five. Here they add up to forty: the value adjustment factor.

afp.text: Adjusted function points: U F P, times zero point six five, plus zero point zero one times V A F. Twenty-three times one point zero five. About twenty-four function points.
